name: Use a fountain pen properly
blurb: Fountain pens want a different grip and much less pressure than a ballpoint. Adjust to that and writing becomes noticeably more comfortable and better looking.
gear: A fountain pen with a fine or medium nib
steps: Learn the grip and angle: hold it lower and at about 45 degrees, with the nib’s tines flat to the paper.
Learn to write with almost no pressure — the ink flows by capillary action and pressing damages the nib.
Learn to fill it properly, whether by converter, cartridge or piston, and to wipe the nib afterwards.
Learn about paper: cheap paper feathers and bleeds, which makes a good pen look bad.
Learn maintenance: flush the pen every few weeks, and always when changing ink.
Write a page a day for a week to adapt your hand to the lighter touch.
tips: Skipping usually means the nib is rotated off its sweet spot, or the pen needs a flush.
Never lend a fountain pen you care about. Nibs wear to one person’s hand.
Do not fly with a full pen at altitude in a bag, or use permanent inks not designed for fountain pens.
proof: A page of comfortable, consistent writing with no skipping, blotting or hand fatigue.
